Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Gradual rollout matrix + docs triage for v2.1

Team —

We need to lock the rollout window and finalize the enablement artifacts for the v2.1 gradual rollout next month. I put a first-pass matrix in the attached rollout_matrix_v1.xlsx and an enablement checklist (enablement_checklist_v0.3.md) that maps owners to deliverables. High-level asks: 

- Confirm rollout cadence (can we do 3 waves over 10 business days?).
- Identify blocking exceptions (security, billing, dedicated-customer flags) that must stop a wave.
- Doc owners: who will own the public release notes vs internal playbook vs CS training?
- Training: agree on the date for a 60-minute enablement for CS & SEs.

Jared/Acme — I’ve included you so you have visibility on timing. We’ll confirm the first wave date after we finalize owners. 

Please review and reply with owner assignments + any hard constraints by EOD Wed (Dec 2). If you see infra gaps, call them out in the matrix (column: infra-risk).

Attachments: rollout_matrix_v1.xlsx (sheet: wave-plan), enablement_checklist_v0.3.md

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. PM, Launch & Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Gradual rollout matrix + docs triage for v2.1

Laura / team —

Quick infra note: our Dedicated pools will be capacity-limited the week of Dec 13 due to a regional maintenance window (see JIRA-OPS-1298). If Acme or other early customers are pinned to dedicated variants, we need to gate them from wave 1 or provide fallback to hosted. I added an infra-risk column in rollout_matrix_v1.xlsx.

On the cadence: 3 waves over 10 business days is feasible but recommend the following gating rule: max 2% of total production traffic per wave (to ensure KV cache warm-up and no downstream spikes). That reduces blast radius and fits existing autoscale policies. If we need higher coverage per wave, we must provision extra capacity for the first 48 hours of the wave.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether the compliance exception list requires additional sign-off for Acme? I believe their contract has an additional data-retention ask.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Gradual rollout matrix + docs triage for v2.1 — decisions and action items

Thanks everyone — summary and action items below. Leaving on the thread so Acme has visibility.

Decisions (as of Thu, Dec 2):
- Cadence: 3 waves over 10 business days (Wave 1 start: Dec 15 tentative).
- Gate: max 2% prod traffic per wave. Any customer needing >2% in wave 1 must be escalated for capacity.
- Owners: Public release notes -> Ben Carter; Internal playbook -> Laura Bennett; CS training slides + session -> Monica Patel (training: Dec 10 11:00–12:00 PT).
- Exceptions: compliance or dedicated-customer retention exceptions will require Legal + Security sign-off; Kimberly Park to maintain exception queue.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Ben Carter: draft public release notes with sample payloads (due Dec 8).
- Marcus Lin: add API sample snippets to internal API doc and confirm dedicated fallback plan (due Dec 4).
- Laura Bennett: finalize internal playbook + link to Drive folder (due Dec 9).
- Monica Patel: prepare training slides and run the session on Dec 10 (due Dec 9).
- Kimberly Park: publish exception review process and maintain exception list in Drive (due Dec 4).
- Evelyn Hart: finalize rollout_matrix_v1.xlsx with infra-risk flags and create the JIRA epic for rollout coordination (done: JIRA-OPS-1298).

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-gradual-rollout (playbook + slides), JIRA-OPS-1298.

Acme/Jared — please flag any constraints on Dec 15 for wave 1. If you need an earlier or later start for your tenant, ping Kimberly for exceptions.

I'll update the matrix after I get Marcus's infra confirmations tomorrow and will post the finalized playbook.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. PM, Launch & Ops
Redwood Inference
